title: NIST ASD: hydrogen 2–4 air wavelength 486.135 nm
summary: The same retrieval lists an unresolved 2–4 line at 486.135 ± 0.005 nm in air, and classified components near 486.129 nm.
body: On the same NIST ASD hydrogen retrieval, the unresolved 2–4 row has observed air wavelength 486.135 nm, uncertainty 0.005 nm, relative intensity 180000, and Einstein A 8.4193 × 10^6 s^−1. Classified rows on the same page include 486.1283363 nm (2s to 4d), 486.1286949 nm (2s to 4p 3/2), 486.1296711 nm (2s to 4s), and 486.1297761 nm (2s to 4p 1/2), each with uncertainty 0.0000024 nm. The page's note on principal-quantum-number lines applies to the 486.135 nm row: unresolved fine structure, wavelengths pertinent to solar-corona observations. The classified rows are a different listing.

sources.title: NIST Atomic Spectra Database, H lines 400–700 nm
sources.author: National Institute of Standards and Technology, Atomic Spectra Database
sources.note: NIST ASD retrieval fetched 2026-11-18. Column header: Observed Wavelength, Air (nm). The page says lines labeled only by principal quantum numbers correspond to unresolved fine structure and that those wavelengths are pertinent to solar-corona observations.
